sections.heading: Default approach
sections.text: For a three-phase grid-tied inverter with an LCL filter, use dq current regulation with PLL-based synchronization and treat resonance damping as a first-class design requirement. The LCL resonance must be damped before pushing current-loop bandwidth.

sections.heading: LCL filter design
sections.text: L1 (inverter side) sized for current ripple 10-25% of rated current at fsw. Cf sized so LCL resonance f_res = 1/(2*pi)*sqrt((L1+L2)/(L1*L2*Cf)) falls between 10*f_grid and fsw/2. L2 (grid side) typically 1/3 to 1/5 of L1.

sections.heading: Active damping
sections.text: Capacitor-current feedback with gain R_d acts as virtual resistor in series with Cf. Starting point: R_d ~ 1/(3*Cf*omega_res). Without active damping, the LCL resonance appears as a sharp peak in the loop gain that destabilizes the current loop.

sections.heading: PLL design
sections.text: PLL bandwidth should be 5-10x below the current-loop bandwidth. For current-loop crossover of fsw/10, set PLL crossover to fsw/100 or lower. In weak grid (SCR < 3), reduce PLL bandwidth further or switch to grid-forming control (VSG/VOC/droop).

sections.heading: dq decoupling
sections.text: The d-axis and q-axis plants are coupled through omega*L cross-terms. Without feedforward decoupling (Vd_ff = -omega*L*Iq, Vq_ff = omega*L*Id), the loops fight each other and effective bandwidth drops by 50% or more.
